name: GitHub
tagline: Register a GitHub OAuth App and plug it into Composio. No review, live in minutes.

switchReasons.title: Your name on the consent screen
switchReasons.detail: Managed shows "Composio wants access". Your app shows your product name.

switchReasons.title: Scopes you choose
switchReasons.detail: Request exactly the scopes your tools need, not Composio's defaults.

switchReasons.title: Faster triggers
switchReasons.detail: Managed apps poll every 15 minutes at most.

requirements.title: GitHub account
requirements.detail: Org owner role if the org should own the app.

requirements.title: Composio project
requirements.detail: Dashboard access to create an auth config.

requirements.title: Public homepage URL
requirements.detail: Required field on the GitHub form. Shown to users.

requirements.title: List of GitHub tools you use

steps.title: Choose who owns the app
pointers: Organization: survives team changes. Needs org owner.
Personal account: fastest. Transfer to an org any time.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth App

fields.label: Authorization callback URL
fields.hint: Must match your Composio auth config exactly

fields.label: Enable Device Flow
fields.hint: Only for CLI or headless sign-in

pointers: Org-owned: github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/applications/new
No review. The app works as soon as it is registered.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
pointers: Shown once. Copy it before leaving the page.
Store it in a secret manager, never in git.
The Client ID is public. The secret is not.

steps.title: Check your Client ID
pointers: Loads GitHub's sign-in page with your Client ID.
Valid ID: page says "continue to <your app name>".

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config

fields.label: Starter scopes
fields.hint: Trim to what your tools need

pointers: Paste the Client ID and client secret.
Redirect URI must match the GitHub callback URL exactly.
Copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
pointers: Toolkits you don't list keep using managed auth.
Your coding agent can paste this in.

steps.title: Connect a test account
pointers: Consent screen shows your app name, not Composio.
Org access section? Grant it, or request it.
Users connected through managed auth must reconnect.

steps.title: Get org approval
steps.when: Only if your users' orgs restrict OAuth apps
pointers: Restrictions are on by default for new orgs.
Users click Request on the consent screen.
An org owner approves. GitHub sets no deadline.

traps.title: Secret is shown once
traps.detail: Lost it? Generate a new one and update the Composio auth config.

traps.title: repo is all or nothing
traps.detail: Full read and write on every private repo. No read-only private scope exists.

traps.title: Callback must match exactly
traps.detail: Composio's redirect URI and GitHub's callback URL must be identical.

traps.title: 10 tokens per user
traps.detail: The 11th token for the same user and scopes revokes an older one.

traps.title: 8-hour tokens
traps.detail: Expiring tokens are on by default. Refresh tokens last 6 months unused.

evidence.note: Composio says it refreshes OAuth tokens. Not tested end to end for GitHub.

traps.title: Some tools need a GitHub App
traps.detail: Check runs and check suites fail with OAuth App tokens.

blockers.title: Your users' org blocks the app
blockers.detail: Private org repos stay hidden until approved.
blockers.fix: User clicks Request. An org owner approves in org settings.

blockers.title: You're not an org owner
blockers.detail: Only owners can register org-owned apps.
blockers.fix: Register under your account, then transfer to the org.
